dales_walker.text: I'm doing the Three Peaks: Pen-y-ghent, Whernside and Ingleborough, twenty-four miles in twelve hours. My knees have said they will do it, and then they will never speak to me again.
Rule one of the Dales is you always say hello to a walker. Rule two is you never go past a gate without closing it. Rule three is the weather changes on the hour.

dales_waller.text: Drystone walling. You pick up a stone, you look at it, you put it down in the right place. Then you do that eleven thousand times and you have a wall.
The middle of a wall is full of small stones called hearting. It's what keeps the big ones standing. Same as most families.

dales_cheesewife.text: Wensleydale cheese: crumbly, mild and good with fruit cake. If you're a Yorkshire person, it's a reasonable thing to say, 'Cheese and cake? Lovely.'
Monks from France first made it here in the twelfth century, and we've been very polite about the recipe ever since.

dales_geologist.text: See the pavement? That's the sea floor of a tropical sea, around 330 million years ago. The fossils in it are corals and shells.
Yes, the same thing that makes the cliff also makes the cheese land. It's all limestone, one way or another.

dales_postie.text: I deliver to farms where the nearest neighbour is a bull. It's the only time in my life I've been relieved to have a van with a lock on it.
There's a farm up the lane where the post box is a stone wall with a hole in it. Nobody's lost a letter yet.
